draftNotes: Hand-written from bixbeiderbecke.com's 1927 sessionography (matrix numbers, studios, solo orders), checked against the CD booklet as transcribed on Discogs. Nine sessions, all in New York: Frank Trumbauer and His Orchestra (Feb 4, May 9, May 13, Aug 25, Sep 28), Tram, Bix and Eddie / Lang (May 13, Sep 17), In a Mist (Bix alone, September), the Broadway Bell-Hops for Harmony (Sep 29), and Trumbauer's band issued on OKeh 40912 as "Benny Meroff and His Orchestra" (Sep 30).

Trumbology has Bix (short breaks) and Howdy Quicksell on banjo, not Eddie Lang, whatever the Apple credit says. On Singin' the Blues Lang replaces Quicksell and Miff Mole replaces Bill Rank (Melody Maker 1934, Trumbauer in Rhythm 1939).

Left out as unconfirmed: Doc Ryker on the February sides (the booklet has him, the sessionography doesn't); Howdy Quicksell on the May sides (the booklet has him, the sessionography has Lang on guitar and banjo and documents his breaks); the second trumpet (Sylvester Ahola or Frank Cush) and the banjo (Lang, who Ahola's diary says was ill from Sep 30) on Just an Hour of Love and I'm Wonderin' Who.
In a Mist is dated September 8 by the sessionography and September 9 by the booklet and Wikipedia, so only the month is kept.

The two versions of There's a Cradle in Caroline (Trumbauer, Aug 25, Seger Ellis singing; Broadway Bell-Hops, Sep 29, Irving Kaufman singing) share a title, and credits are matched by title, so each version's players show on both.
The app's Apple Music match was Black Radio 2 (2013); corrected to Black Radio (2012) in catalog.json.

The single, Watermelon Man and Don't Bother Me No More (Battle 45909), is from December 17, 1962; the other ten studio tracks from February 18 and 20, 1963, all at Plaza Sound. Mauricio Smith's flute is on The Boogie Cha-Cha Blues and Suavito; Mongo plays bongo on Yeh-Yeh.

The drummer on the single is disputed: the CD credits and jazzdisco's older listing have Frank Hernandez and Kalil Madi, the current jazzdisco listing and Gerard's Music from Cuba have Ray Lucas, so nobody is credited on drums for those two tracks. La Lupe's vocal effects on Watermelon Man are on the CD credits only and are left out.
The six live bonus tracks are Mongo's earlier band at the Blackhawk, San Francisco, dated 1962 by both sources with no day.
